Frequently Asked Questions

Tax, Zakat & ZATCA FAQs

Both are administered by ZATCA, but they apply on different bases and to different categories of ownership. Zakat generally applies to Saudi and GCC ownership and is calculated on a Zakat base, while corporate income tax generally applies to non-GCC ownership and is calculated on taxable profit. Entities with mixed ownership may be subject to both, apportioned according to the ownership profile. The treatment for any specific company should be confirmed against its own facts.

Zakat obligations generally arise for entities owned by Saudi and GCC nationals, including companies where such ownership forms part of a mixed shareholding. Whether an obligation applies, and how the Zakat base is determined, depends on the legal form, ownership structure and activities of the entity. We review these factors before confirming the position.

VAT registration requirements are linked to the value of a business's taxable supplies over a defined period, with mandatory and voluntary registration thresholds set by the regulations. Non-resident businesses making taxable supplies in Saudi Arabia may face different requirements. We assess turnover, activity type and residency status against the current rules to confirm whether registration is required.

Withholding tax applies to certain payments made by a resident party to a non-resident for services or other categories of income sourced in Saudi Arabia. The applicable rate depends on how the payment is classified, and a relevant double-tax treaty may affect the outcome. Correct classification of the payment is usually the most important step, and we support this alongside calculation and filing.

Transfer pricing requirements generally apply to entities that transact with related persons or under controlled conditions. Obligations may include an annual disclosure form together with documentation such as a local file and master file, with the applicable requirements depending on the size of the entity and the value of its controlled transactions. We assess the transactions in scope and confirm which requirements apply.

FATOORA is the Saudi e-invoicing programme. Phase 2, the integration phase, requires taxpayers to connect their invoicing systems with ZATCA's platform so that invoices are cleared or reported in the prescribed technical format. Taxpayers are notified of their integration wave by ZATCA. We support readiness assessment, invoice and system review, and coordination of the integration.
